q: Density is the ratio of mass to volume of a substance.
e: True. Density is the ratio of mass to volume of a substance. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: Density is the ratio of volume to mass of a substance.
e: False. Density is the ratio of mass to volume of a substance. This claim used to mass in place of mass to.

q: Density is the scalar quantity.
e: True. Density is the scalar quantity. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: Density is the vector quantity.
e: False. Density is the scalar quantity. This claim used vector in place of scalar.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$).
e: True. In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$).
e: False. In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: In CGS unit, it is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or gram per millilitre ($\text{g mL}^{-1}$).
e: True. In CGS unit, it is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or gram per millilitre ($\text{g mL}^{-1}$). In CGS unit is an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement.

q: In CGS unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$).
e: False. In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$). This claim used CGS in place of SI.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a balance.
e: True. Mass of an object can be measured using a balance. Mass of an object can be measured using a balance is the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a measuring cylinder.
e: False. Volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder.

q: Volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder.
e: True. Volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder. Every quantity named in that sentence is being used in its physics sense.

q: Volume can be measured using a balance.
e: False. Volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder. This claim used balance in place of measuring cylinder.

q: Mass of the object does not change, but the volume depends on the temperature.
e: True. Mass of the object does not change, but the volume depends on the temperature. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Mass of the object changes with temperature, but the volume does not change.
e: False. Mass of the object does not change, but the volume depends on the temperature. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.
